name: Sean Pitt
profile: Former SpaceX sales executive who led launch and human-spaceflight sales in Europe (over $1.25B in export deals) before co-founding Castelion in November 2022 with Bryon Hargis and Andrew Kreitz. As COO he runs operations and programme execution for Castelion's low-cost hypersonic strike systems; its Blackbeard missile is a Navy programme of record, and the company was valued at about $13B in late 2026.
interesting_fact: When the founders told the Pentagon's Defense Innovation Unit they would compete with Lockheed Martin, the room laughed. Castelion's first Navy contract was $3M, and it has since won over $500M in US government contracts.
deep_cut_fact: He was the original salesperson for SpaceX's rideshare programme, which went on to be hugely successful, and was a SpaceX spokesperson in his 20s. He recalls that Castelion's first poster carried the tagline 'Win before it begins.'
notes: Sales and communications background makes him a natural interviewee. The poster tagline and his spokesperson role come from Fortune (Oct 2026); the rideshare detail comes from TechCrunch (2023). Press route: media@castelion.com.

name: Alex Carges
current_role: Co-founder & Head of Insurance (Product), Nirvana Insurance
profile: Credentialed property-casualty actuary (FCAS) who was chief actuary at insurtech Root Insurance and earlier worked at The Hartford, before co-founding Nirvana Insurance in 2021 with Rushil Goel and Abhay Mitra. He leads insurance product and pricing at Nirvana, which uses truck telematics data to underwrite commercial trucking insurance and raised a $100M Series D at a $1.5B valuation in December 2025.
interesting_fact: Nirvana sold its first policy in 2022 and was named the fastest-growing insurtech within its first year.
deep_cut_fact: As Root Insurance's chief actuary he appeared on the actuarial 'Not Unreasonable Podcast' (Aug 2020, 'Actuaries and Data Scientists at Root'), debating whether territory and technology really matter in auto pricing and actuaries vs data scientists - the data-driven pricing approach he now applies to trucking.
notes: Low media profile; insurance and actuarial specialist. Career dates (Root 2017-2020, The Hartford, Allied World) come from profile aggregators. Route via Nirvana press.

name: Chai Xiaojie
profile: PhD engineer with about 15 years in robotics and autonomous driving, including taking L4 self-driving products into mass production, who co-founded embodied-AI startup PsiBot in September 2024 with CEO Wang Qibin. He brings algorithms, simulation and full-stack engineering skills to PsiBot's reinforcement-learning manipulation models and dexterous hands; Bloomberg reported a $1.48B valuation in July 2026.
interesting_fact: PsiBot's robots, running its Psi R1 model, were shown playing mahjong autonomously, deciding when to pong, kong and declare a winning hand.
deep_cut_fact: PsiBot's founders call themselves the '7890 team' (7890战队) because they span four decades of birth years: 1970s-born CEO Wang Qibin, Chai as the 1980s-born 'algorithm veteran', 1990s-born Peking University scholar Yang Yaodong and 2000s-born Chen Yuanpei.
notes: Very low public profile; background is documented only in Chinese funding coverage (QbitAI, Nov 2024: https://www.qbitai.com/2024/11/218183.html). Route via the company.

name: Chad Larson
current_role: Co-founder of M-KOPA (left the company in 2018); most recently listed as Chief Credit Risk Officer at Moniepoint (as of 2023)
profile: American former investment banker (CFA, Oxford MBA) who co-founded M-KOPA in Nairobi in 2010-11 with Nick Hughes and Jesse Moore and served as its finance director and chief credit officer, building the pay-as-you-go credit model behind solar power for over a million East African homes. He later ran Kenyan payments firm Kopo Kopo until its acquisition by Moniepoint, then became Moniepoint's chief credit risk officer.
interesting_fact: M-KOPA's daily-repayment credit model, which he helped design, first brought pay-as-you-go solar to more than a million off-grid East African homes and later expanded into smartphone financing.
deep_cut_fact: Before Africa he spent 10 years in investment banking at Bank of America in Sydney and New York (fixed income, structured finance, derivatives), then was CFO of the AfriCap Microfinance Investment Fund in Johannesburg before co-founding M-KOPA.
notes: Has been in a public dispute with M-KOPA since 2025 over its employee-share programme (the company says he left in 2018 and holds about 1%), so do not route outreach through M-KOPA. His Moniepoint role is from a 2023 speaker bio and may be out of date. No self-published contact found.
